section.title: High-Level Architecture
section.description: - Section 4 answers "what is the system MADE OF" — the cross-cutting picture: overall topology, the technology stack, and external integrations. State each of these ONCE here. - It does NOT describe how an individual feature uses that stack — that is Section 7.3 (the vertical slice of each feature through UI → API → Data). Section 7.3 *uses* what Section 4 declares; it must not re-declare or fork the stack. - Keep system-wide planning facts here so the PRD has one source before handoff: if the same fact (e.g., the auth mechanism, the database choice) also appears per-feature in Section 7.3, the PRD drifts internally. `/feature-to-adr` later transfers durable contracts and boundaries into ADRs and classifies replaceable technology means as code discretion. After successful handoff, ADRs are the implementation authority and this section may remain as legacy planning context.

subsection.title: System Diagram
subsection.description: - Provide both a Context diagram and a Container diagram using Mermaid C4 syntax. - The Context diagram is required. Show the people, external systems, the target system, and their relationships. - The Container diagram is required. Show the major independently running or deployable applications and data stores inside the target system, their responsibilities, technologies at category level, and their relationships. - These are the only C4 levels allowed in an ALPS PRD. Do not generate Component, Dynamic, Deployment, or Code-level C4 diagrams. - Keep modules, classes, functions, files, methods, and other implementation details out of both diagrams.
subsection.example:
```mermaid C4Context
title System Context Diagram for Document Assistant
Person(author, "Document Author", "Creates a product document through conversation") System(documentAssistant, "Document Assistant", "Guides the author and produces the document") System_Ext(llm, "LLM Service", "Generates guided questions and draft content")
Rel(author, documentAssistant, "Authors a document with") Rel(documentAssistant, llm, "Requests language generation from") ```
```mermaid C4Container
title Container Diagram for Document Assistant
Person(author, "Document Author", "Creates a product document through conversation") System_Ext(llm, "LLM Service", "Generates guided questions and draft content")
System_Boundary(documentAssistant, "Document Assistant") { Container(webApp, "Web Application", "Web UI", "Runs the guided authoring conversation") Container(api, "Application API", "Server application", "Manages the authoring workflow and document state") ContainerDb(documentStore, "Document Store", "Persistent storage", "Stores approved product documents") }
Rel(author, webApp, "Uses") Rel(webApp, api, "Sends approved section content to") Rel(api, documentStore, "Reads and writes") Rel(api, llm, "Requests language generation from") ```

subsection.title: Technology Stack
subsection.description: - List the key technologies and frameworks to be used in the MVP. - If the user is non-technical, follow the tech_stack_wizard in the section guide to help them choose. - Cover these categories as applicable: - Frontend: How users interact with the product (e.g., web framework, mobile framework) - Backend: Server-side logic and APIs (e.g., language, framework) - Database: Where data is stored (e.g., relational, document-based) - Infrastructure: Where the product runs and how it is deployed (e.g., cloud provider, CI/CD) - External Services: Third-party APIs or services (e.g., payment, email, AI/ML) - Not all categories are required — include only what is relevant to the MVP. - Record the expected launch scale that drove this choice as a one-line "Scale assumption". Write it down rather than leaving it in the conversation: it is the main driver behind the stack, and Section 6.2 reuses it as the starting point for the performance NFR. Distinguish total from concurrent users when both are known. - Infer a recommended replaceable stack and pragmatic MVP scale from the approved product context before asking. Mark user-unsupplied choices as `AI-inferred` with their basis in the approval digest. Ask only when a missing constraint materially changes the boundary, provider, security posture, deployment topology, cost, or required scale.
subsection.example: - Scale assumption: ~1,000 total users at launch, tens concurrent at peak - Frontend: React (Tailwind CSS) - Backend: Node.js (Express) - Database: MongoDB - Infrastructure: AWS (EC2), GitHub Actions (CI/CD)
